title: How does one wrong count change a mean?
description: The mean harvest of fifteen trees is known, but one tree's count was written three more than the actual. The mean gives the total, the total is corrected, and the new total gives the correct mean. Keeko doubts this and takes three off the mean itself.
teaching_notes: One idea: turn the mean into a total, correct the total, then divide by the number of values again. Watch for students who subtract the error directly from the mean.

source: The mean harvest of 15 trees is 25.6, but one count was written 3 more than the actual. Find the correct mean.
video_script.why: A child who finds a mean from a list learns to correct a mean when one value was recorded wrongly.
video_script.substitution: the book's coconut farm with fifteen trees, the mean 25.6 and the count that is 3 too high
video_script.anchor: a row of fifteen coconut trees with the mean 25.6 above them
video_script.wrong_answer: the correct mean is twenty two point six
video_script.wrong_move: subtracts the error 3 from the mean itself, though the error is in only one of the 15 counts
video_script.payoff_line: The correct mean is twenty five point four coconuts

final_answer.spoken: the correct mean is twenty five point four coconuts

names.{{NAME_2}}: coconut farmer who averages the harvest of the trees

never_show: 22.6 as the correct mean marked as right
maths_rules: mean = total ÷ number of trees, so total = mean × number of trees
video_script.design: One row of fifteen trees all video. The mean turns into a total, one count is lowered by three, and the total turns back into a mean. Keeko's wrong idea is to take three off the mean.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='farm'/>{{NAME_2}} keeps track of the coconut harvest of fifteen trees on the farm.
<bookmark mark='mean'/>The mean harvest of a tree is twenty five point six.
<bookmark mark='error'/>The son of {{NAME_2}} checks the counts. One tree's count was written three more than the actual. What is the correct mean?

beats.on_screen: the trees and the question stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the line mean = total ÷ number of trees; the same line turned around: total = mean × number of trees; the counts of the trees are not given

marks.rule: the line mean = total ÷ number of trees appears
marks.turn: the line turns around into total = mean × number of trees
marks.hidden: the counts of the trees stay hidden behind a cloth

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The mean is the total harvest divided by the number of trees.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Turn it around, and the total is the mean multiplied by the number of trees.
<bookmark mark='hidden'/>The count of each tree is not given, but the total can still be found.

beats.on_screen: Given: 15 trees, mean = 25.6; one count is 3 more than the actual

marks.given: the number of trees, the mean and the error are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are fifteen trees and the mean is twenty five point six. One count is three more than the actual.

marks.find: the words the correct mean are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the correct mean harvest.
<bookmark mark='times'/>Step one, turn the mean into the total harvest as noted. Multiply twenty five point six by fifteen.
<bookmark mark='total'/>The total as noted is three hundred and eighty four.

marks.fix: 3 is taken away from the total 384

narration: <bookmark mark='fix'/>Step two, fix the total. One count was three too high, so the total is three too high.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Three hundred and eighty four take away three leaves three hundred and eighty one.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Step three, divide the correct total by the number of trees.
<bookmark mark='mean'/>Three hundred and eighty one divided by fifteen gives twenty five point four.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check the result. The three came from one tree, shared among fifteen trees, which is nought point two.
<bookmark mark='drop'/>The mean falls by nought point two, so twenty five point six becomes twenty five point four.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The correct mean is twenty five point four coconuts.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the row of trees
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 25.6 − 3 = 22.6; 22.6 × 15 = 339 is compared with the real total 381; the bubble is struck out

marks.test: 22.6 × 15 = 339 is written beside the real total 381
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 3 is shown leaving only one tree

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the correct mean is twenty two point six, because three is taken off the mean.
<bookmark mark='test'/>But twenty two point six times fifteen is three hundred and thirty nine.
The correct total is three hundred and eighty one, so that cannot be right.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The three was too high on one tree only, not on all fifteen. It comes off the total, not off the mean.
